findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either state the per-status `detail` content (one example string per branch) and add it to the AC7 assertions, or explicitly mark `detail` as advisory/untested free text in the Diagnostic contract.
evidence: 'given a dict it records a `status` plus a human `detail`'
AC7 asserts only `coverage["overlap"]["status"]` records the status, never `detail`
The closed status set is fully specified and tested; `detail` has no stated template or covering criterion
findings.finding: The diagnostics dict records a 'human detail' alongside status, but no acceptance criterion verifies detail and its content/provenance is left unspecified.
findings.location: Approach — 'Diagnostic contract' paragraph; AC line 'Degradation, one test per status'
scenarios: An operator reads coverage['overlap']['detail'] expecting a stable/parseable message but its format was never fixed or tested
A later consumer depends on detail text that drifts
findings.suggested_fix: In the Diagnostic contract, give one example `detail` string per status value and extend AC7 to assert detail is non-empty per status; or state 'detail is advisory free text, not asserted'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify what actually gates the project.plan-overlap criterion ON/OFF per run (tie activation or finder-skip to the overlap flag), since overlay `activate` makes the criterion always-active and the overlap boolean only controls context injection.
evidence: Plan: 'The switch is one keyword-only parameter overlap: bool = False ... threaded exactly as probe_criteria is'
Plan ties degradation/empty-list to non-ok STATUS only, not to overlap=False: 'On any non-ok status the candidate list is empty, no overlap finding is emitted'
criteria/overlay.py:447 'activating a built-in is a no-op (built-ins are always active)' and :427-455 activation makes a project id active for the review type
registry.applies() (registry.py:392-420) filters on scope/suppress_types/require_parent_id only — no per-run overlap flag
production_batch_runner _project_criteria (:281-290) fans in every activated project.* id; the probe allowlist is empty on a normal review so it is not filtered out
findings.finding: The off switch described for AC3 (`overlap=False` emits no overlap finding) is not achieved by the threaded `overlap` boolean: once `project.plan-overlap` is activated in `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` it is always selected and run as a single-turn finder regardless of the flag (overlay activation, not a per-run gate), and `registry.applies()` has no `overlap` axis. The flag only suppresses the injected candidate block via `_chunk_extra_context`; nothing in the mechanism prevents the in-rubric `project.plan-overlap` finder from emitting an overlap finding from the plan text alone when `overlap=False`.
findings.location: Approach: 'On demand, not on every review' + 'Degradation'; AC3
scenarios: overlap=False on a review of a ticket in scope: project.plan-overlap still runs as a single-turn finder with no injected candidate block
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) gate finding emission on the injected block — make the finder's rubric/prompt return no finding when no POSSIBLE OVERLAP block is present (so overlap=False ⇒ empty block ⇒ no candidates ⇒ no finding), and state this invariant explicitly; or (b) keep the criterion inert when overlap=False by routing-level suppression. State which, and how the finder behaves when its id is in-rubric but no block was injected.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the byte-identical-checkpoint-identity AC with overlay activation: either exclude project.plan-overlap from the chunk rubric/topology when overlap=False, or re-scope AC3 to 'identity differs only in the context_digest of the overlap-carrying chunk' and justify why that still satisfies the off-switch intent.
evidence: Plan: 'the run's checkpoint identity stays byte-identical to the same review before this change' (AC3, overlap=False)
checkpoints.py:60-66 prompt_id = 'plan-review:' + ','.join(sorted ids); identity changes with the criterion set
pass1.py:296-302 topology_digest binds chunks/agent/container composition; adding a selected criterion changes it
The overlap flag does not control selection (prior finding) — so the only way to keep overlap=False identity-identical is for the criterion to not be selected when overlap=False
findings.finding: AC3's byte-identical checkpoint-identity requirement conflicts with activating a new criterion. Checkpoint identity binds prompt_id = 'plan-review:'+sorted(criterion ids) and the topology digest; activating `project.plan-overlap` adds its id to a chunk's rubric, changing prompt_id and topology for that chunk. That change occurs at activation time, independent of the overlap flag, so a review with overlap=False after this change cannot have byte-identical checkpoint identity to the same review before the change (the rubric now contains project.plan-overlap).
findings.location: Approach: 'Riding it rather than adding a pass leaves checkpoint identity plus caching unchanged'; AC3
scenarios: Comparing checkpoint identity of a pre-change review vs. a post-change overlap=False review, once project.plan-overlap is activated
findings.suggested_fix: Decide whether project.plan-overlap is in the rubric at all when overlap=False. If it must be absent for identity-equality, gate its selection on the overlap input (not just context injection); if it is always present, change AC3 to assert identity equality between overlap=False-before and overlap=False-after (both with the criterion active) rather than against the pre-change review.

findings.checklist_item: Specify how the per-candidate `diagnostics` status produced inside the _chunk worker (via _chunk_extra_context → overlap.py → find_similar) propagates to coverage['overlap'] in run_pass1's serial frame, and the reconciliation rule if the criterion appears in more than one chunk.
evidence: Plan: 'coverage["overlap"] is written the same way' as coverage['isf'] (:473) and coverage['recall_candidates'] (:521).
Verified pass1.py:473 and :521 are written in the SERIAL tail of run_pass1, after the worker pool.

Plan: overlap retrieval 'plus its diagnostic live in a new overlap.py'; '_chunk_extra_context gains only the call' — and _chunk_extra_context is invoked at pass1.py:326 INSIDE _chunk, which fans out concurrently (pass1.py:371 max_workers, :388-408 concurrent batch).

The find_similar diagnostics dict (plan's 'Diagnostic contract') is populated inside that worker; the plan gives no mechanism carrying `status` from the worker-local dict up to coverage['overlap'] in the serial frame, nor a rule for reconciling writes if the plan-overlap criterion ever co-chunks or appears in more than one chunk.
findings.finding: The overlap diagnostic status is produced inside a Pass-1 pool worker but recorded into coverage['overlap'] in the serial frame, and the plan does not specify the propagation path — the placement of this state write is ambiguous.
findings.location: Approach → 'Recording channel: coverage, written in place'; pass1.py:326 (call site inside _chunk worker) vs pass1.py:473/:521 (serial coverage writes)
scenarios: Degradation AC: a test asserts coverage['overlap']['status'] == 'catch-up-failed' after a worker-run retrieval fails; without a defined propagation seam the key may never be set.
A future chunking change places project.plan-overlap in more than one chunk, producing concurrent worker writes to the same coverage key with no specified last-writer/merge rule.
findings.suggested_fix: State that overlap.py returns the diagnostics dict to _chunk_extra_context's caller, and that run_pass1 assigns coverage['overlap'] = {status, detail} AFTER the worker pool joins (same serial position as coverage['isf']:473), explicitly from the chunk carrying project.plan-overlap; note that exactly one chunk carries it so there is a single writer.
